## Branch
```
v2
```

> ⚠️ **WARNING — BRANCH RULE**
> This issue must be worked on and submitted **only** from the `v2` branch.
> Pull requests targeting any other branch will **not be merged**.
> `git checkout v2 && git checkout -b your-name/v2-referral-leaderboard`

## Summary
Extend referrals (Issue 15) with tiered reward multipliers, a public leaderboard, monthly contests with prize distribution, and a referral analytics dashboard.

## What Needs to Be Done

### 1. ReferralTier entity
Seeded: Bronze (0 referrals, 1x), Silver (10, 1.25x), Gold (25, 1.5x), Platinum (50, 2x). Add `referralTier` and `referralCount` to User. Auto-upgrade on each successful referral reward.

### 2. Tiered reward
Base 5 XLM × tier multiplier. Multiplier stored on Referral entity at reward time for auditability.

### 3. Leaderboard
`GET /v2/referrals/leaderboard?period=alltime|month` — top 50 by count. Shows `{ rank, displayName (first + last initial), count, tier, rewardEarned }`. Always includes user's own rank even outside top 50. Cache: 1h alltime, 5min monthly.

### 4. Monthly contest
`ReferralContest` entity: name, startDate, endDate, prizes (jsonb: `[{ rank, rewardXlm }]`). Cron on end date: rank participants, credit prizes via ledger, notify winners.

### 5. Admin
`GET /admin/referrals/stats`, `POST /admin/referral-tiers`, `POST /admin/referral-contests`, `PATCH /admin/referral-contests/:id/complete`

### 6. User dashboard
`GET /v2/referrals/me`: tier, count, total earned, next tier progress %, referral link

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Gold tier (25 referrals) earns 7.5 XLM per referral (1.5x)
- [ ] Leaderboard top-50 with user's own rank always present
- [ ] Cache used — DB not queried on every leaderboard request
- [ ] Contest end triggers prize distribution; winners notified
- [ ] Tier auto-upgrades when count crosses threshold
- [ ] Prize distribution uses ledger — not direct balance write

## Constraints
- Leaderboard shows first name + last initial only — no full name or email
- Complexity: **High — 200 points**
title: [Wave 200pts] v2: Referral leaderboard and tier rewards — multipliers, monthly contests, prize distribution, and analytics

## Description

Test `finalizeTournament()` prize distribution for all participant count scenarios: 0 scores, 1 player, 2 players, and 3+ players.

## Context

Prize distribution rules:
- **1 participant**: 100% of pool
- **2 participants**: 1st=70%, 2nd=30%
- **3+ participants**: 1st=60%, 2nd=25%, 3rd=15% (dust to 1st)
- **0 scores**: no distribution, event with `winner=address(0)`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] 1 participant: `claimablePrize[id][player] == prizePool`
- [ ] 2 participants: 1st = `(pool * 7000) / 10000`, 2nd = `pool - first`
- [ ] 3 participants: 1st=60%, 2nd=25%, 3rd=15%, any dust added to 1st
- [ ] 0 scores submitted: emits finalized event with winner=address(0), prizeAmount=0
- [ ] Reverts before `endTime` → `TournamentNotEnded()`
- [ ] Reverts on double finalization → `TournamentAlreadyFinalized()`
- [ ] `tournament.winner` and `winningScore` match `leaderboard[0]`
- [ ] `tournament.status == Finalized` after call
- [ ] Verify exact wei amounts for a pool of `10e18` with 5 participants

## Files to Modify

- `test/CeloFlashTournament.test.js`

## Difficulty: 🔴 Hard

## Problem

There is no discovery mechanism for popular or high-value raffles. Users browsing for raffles must enumerate all instances with no ranking signal.

## Design

Add leaderboard tracking to the factory. Update on every finalization callback:

```rust
DataKey::TopByTickets   // Vec<(Address, u32)> top 10 by tickets_sold
DataKey::TopByPrize     // Vec<(Address, i128)> top 10 by prize_amount
DataKey::TopByVolume    // Vec<(Address, i128)> top 10 by total ticket revenue
```

New factory function:

```rust
pub fn get_leaderboard(env: Env, metric: LeaderboardMetric) -> Vec<(Address, i128)>

pub enum LeaderboardMetric {
    TicketsSold = 0,
    PrizeAmount = 1,
    TotalVolume = 2,
}
```

Leaderboards are updated when a raffle finalizes (via callback from instance) or can be submitted by anyone for a specific raffle with on-chain verification.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Leaderboard top-10 is maintained and queryable
- [ ] Inserting a new top-10 raffle evicts the smallest existing entry
- [ ] Leaderboard updates are O(10) — not O(total raffles)
- [ ] Test: create 15 raffles with varying ticket counts, verify top-10 is correct
title: [FEATURE] Implement on-chain raffle leaderboard — track most tickets sold and biggest prizes

## Context
This is a direct follow-up to **Issue #44** (Circles v2). Now that circles are decoupled from individual books and support sequential reading, we can introduce high-engagement timed reading competitions with real Lightning Network payouts!

## Problem
While general reading leaderboards are fun, long-term reading can lose momentum. Short-term, high-stakes gamified competitions with real monetary incentives (Bitcoin/sats) provide a powerful social dynamic to drive engagement and ensure book comprehension.

## Proposed solution

Implement **Competition Mode** for Circles. This allows an admin or host to create structured timed challenges within a circle, featuring progress leaderboards, custom reading comprehension quizzes, and automated Lightning prize distributions.

### 1. Competition Setup (Admin Flow)
- Circle admins/hosts can click **"Create Competition"** within a Circle V2 page.
- **Parameters to define**:
  - **Duration**: (e.g., 5 days, 1 week).
  - **Target Reading**: Specific chapters, pages, or entire books.
  - **Prize Pool**: Reward amount in satoshis (e.g., 5000 sats), members can contribute to prize pool "fund raise" where the winner takes it.
  - **Quizzes**: Admins can author multiple-choice Q/As or leverage `QuizService` to pre-generate reading comprehension questions.

### 2. Joining & Leaderboard Tracking
- Circle members see a highly polished prompt/banner on their Circle dashboard: *"Join the 5-Day Reading Challenge! Prize: 2,500 Sats!"*.
- Clicking **"Join"** enrolls them in the challenge.
- A specialized **Competition Leaderboard** is established, ranking enrolled members using a composite score formula:
  59\text{Score} = \text{Reading Progress Points} + \text{Quiz Accuracy Points} + \text{Speed Bonuses}59

### 3. Daily / End-of-Competition Quizzes
- At the end of each designated reading day, participants receive a push notification/in-app sheet to take the **"Daily Comprehension Quiz"**.
- The quizzes verify that the reader actually understood the target content (not just scrolled through pages).
- Scores are tallied in real-time and appended to the competition leaderboard.

### 4. Automated Winner Declaration & Sats Prize Payout
- Once the competition timer expires and all quizzes are completed:
  1. The app automatically tallies final scores and declares the winner(s).
  2. The app **generates a Lightning invoice** on behalf of the winner (using their registered `lud16` address).
  3. The admin/host is prompted with a **"Pay Winner"** modal.
  4. The host can pay the invoice instantly via their connected NWC (Nostr Wallet Connect) wallet or by scanning the generated invoice QR code.
  5. A celebration sheet triggers for all circle members, announcing the winner and the prize payout event.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Admin creation interface for scheduling circle competitions with custom durations and custom quizzes.
- [ ] "Join Competition" prompt banner visible to all circle members.
- [ ] Score calculation and sorting logic based on reading progress and quiz correct answers.
- [ ] Push/in-app prompt surfacing quizzes to active competitors at the correct times.
- [ ] Winning payout flow: automatically query the winner's `lud16`, request an invoice, and display a one-click "Pay Prize" action to the competition host.
title: [Feature]: Circle Competition Mode (Timed Challenges, Quizzes, and Lightning Sats Prize payouts)

This issue is the **framing + design-discussion doc** for adapting [guild-hall](https://github.com/cgbarlow/guild-hall) (forked here as `unsorry-guild`) into an engagement layer for the [unsorry](https://github.com/agenticsnz/unsorry) swarm. It captures the direction that's been set and what's still open. Comment inline; decisions get folded back up into this issue.

> ### Related unsorry work — the credit model this guild rides on
> This guild's prizes and leaderboards are an engagement-layer view of unsorry's **board/credit model**, which is actively being reformed by two merged "Proposed" ADRs (both follow discussion [unsorry#3217](https://github.com/agenticsnz/unsorry/discussions/3217) and defer provenance to ADR-023/037 — the leaderboard/provenance spec this guild already reads from):
> - **ADR-078 — sponsor-registered targets & obligation-discharge credit** ([unsorry#3232](https://github.com/agenticsnz/unsorry/pull/3232)): moves the unit of board credit from standalone atoms to *credited obligations discharged within sponsor-registered targets* (board credit = credited obligations + targets completed, statement-hash deduped, self-target = 0; trivially-closable nodes are "glue" and earn zero; the decomposition skeleton is sponsor-authored and immutable). **This is the closest unsorry concept to our "prize":** a guild prize is effectively the engagement-layer face of a sponsor-registered target, and per-prize ranking should count ADR-078 credited obligations rather than raw atom/proof counts.
> - **ADR-079 — deterministic solver provider** ([unsorry#3246](https://github.com/agenticsnz/unsorry/pull/3246)): adds an optional sympy provider with a **board-submission guard** — deterministically-farmable easy goals can't earn board credit without a credit-reform attestation. The guild's leaderboards/prizes must **honor the same guard** so a proof-factory can't top a prize board.
> **Net:** the score basis in Decision #3 (`difficulty_points×100 + proofs×25`, ADR-023) is the *current* board formula and is itself being reformed — the guild should track the **ADR-023 → ADR-078 → ADR-079** credit chain rather than hard-code today's formula. See **Decision #3** and **Open items** below.

## Why we're doing this

unsorry is a swarm that proves theorems. We want to **encourage contributors in the swarm to work toward specified goals**, and the lever is engagement: present goals as **prizes / badges**, run **leaderboards** per goal, and award **badges** that live on contributor profiles. guild-hall already is a "quest → badge → leaderboard → profile" engine, so we fork it and bend it to point at unsorry's goals instead of generic quests. Secondarily, `unsorry-guild` becomes the new home for unsorry's existing public pages (leaderboard, showcase, proof graph, queue).

## What each side gives us (grounding)

**guild-hall today** (Next.js 15 App Router + Supabase + Netlify, TanStack Query, shadcn/ui):
- A full **quest → objective → points → achievement/badge → tier → leaderboard → profile** model in Supabase (~24 tables, 140+ migrations). Achievements already support criteria types `quest_count` / `points_total` / `streak` / `manual` (`supabase/migrations/010_achievements.sql`).
- A **privacy-respecting leaderboard** computed as a Postgres view (`supabase/migrations/060_view_leaderboard.sql`).
- **Auth** via Supabase (email/password + Google/Apple OAuth), roles `admin` / `gm` / `member`, middleware-protected routes (`src/middleware.ts`, `src/lib/auth/`), plus a lot of email/onboarding/digest surface.
- A **categories** table + per-quest filter dropdown (`supabase/migrations/004_*`, `src/components/quests/quest-filters.tsx`) — the closest existing thing to a "domain" filter, but it's per-quest, not a site-wide context.
- Theming: `light` / `warm` / `dark`; default is currently `warm` (`src/app/layout.tsx`). Dark already exists as a full theme.

**unsorry today** (the data we'd point at):
- **Identity = GitHub username.** Contributors are credited via `solver≜<handle>` provenance records in `library/index/*.aisp` (ADR-023). No emails, no accounts, no real names.
- **The repo is the database.** Goals (`goals/*.aisp`), proofs (`library/Unsorry/*.lean`), proof metadata (`library/index/*.aisp`), run facts (`proof-runs/*.aisp`) and commit history are the single source of truth.
- The **four pages** (`docs/leaderboard.html`, `docs/showcase.html`, `docs/proofs-contributors-visualisation.html` + `proof-graph.svg`, `docs/queue.html`) are static HTML+Tailwind+vanilla-JS, **generated by GitHub Actions** (`tools/leaderboard`, `tools/visualiser`, `tools/queue_board`) into JSON artifacts (`docs/metrics/*.json`) and served from **GitHub Pages**. Queue is live from `queued/prove/*` branches + the GitHub PR API.
- **No formal goals/prizes system** — just a worklist (`docs/targets.md`) and a difficulty-weighted leaderboard (`score = difficulty_points*100 + verified_proofs*25`, ADR-023).
- **ADR-030** (the domain-agnostic workload engine, roadmap Phase 6, **not yet started**): a "domain" is a plugin implementing `generate/verify/decompose/assimilate`, with verifiability tiers `VERIFIED` / `SCORED` / `CONSENSUS`. **Math = Lean = VERIFIED**, and is the only domain that exists.

## Decisions

1. **Auth & identity → admin-only, GitHub everywhere else.** Strip the email/password + OAuth login, registration, onboarding, and email/digest machinery; the only authenticated role is **admin** (Supabase auth). Everyone else is anonymous, public, read-only. Contributors are **GitHub handles**, auto-sourced from unsorry's git provenance (no signup); profiles are keyed on the handle (e.g. `/u/<handle>`). guild-hall's quest lifecycle (accept → submit-evidence → GM-review) is **removed** — completion is git-verified. **Admin scope:** define prizes & criteria, run seasons (open/close + confirm the podium), grant manual/discretionary badges, and curate content (showcase, banners, featured proofs). _(Blast radius: `src/lib/auth/`, `src/middleware.ts`, email-preference tables, RLS policies, `user_quests`/`user_objectives`/evidence/GM-review.)_

2. **Data architecture → slim Supabase overlay over git.** **git is the source of truth**: all proof / contributor / leaderboard data is read from unsorry's git artifacts. A **slim Supabase overlay** holds only the guild-specific concepts that don't exist in unsorry's git — prize definitions, completion criteria, awards/podium results, and admin-curated content. Computed standings & badge-eligibility are **recomputed from the git artifacts on read (short cache)**, not persisted; the overlay stores only authored config plus **frozen closed-season results**.

3. **Prizes = flagship targets, difficulty-weighted & seasoned.** A prize is a **flagship target** — a headline goal (`goal id`) plus its dependency / sub-lemma tree — and there can be **multiple** flagship targets running at once. Clicking a prize opens its **own per-prize leaderboard**, ranking contributors by **difficulty-weighted discharge** (`difficulty_points×100 + credited_proofs×25`, ADR-023, tracking the ADR-023 → 078 → 079 chain) of that target's tree. The **season closes when the target's headline goal is proved**; the admin then **confirms the podium** (**1st / 2nd / 3rd**), with **"contributor"** for anyone with ≥1 proof in the tree. Each prize shows a **live progress indicator** toward completion (% of the target's tree discharged + a target-scoped proof-graph/dependency view, reusing unsorry's proof-graph data). Badges land on the contributor's **profile** (reusing guild-hall's badge/profile UI). **Attribution plumbing:** `swarm/run.sh` and `swarm/agent.sh` already accept `--goal <id>`; extend this to **target-awareness** (a `--target <id>` spanning the target's goal set) across `swarm/run.sh` / `agent.sh` / `sourcing.sh` so a contributor can flag from the CLI which flagship target they're working toward — that flag is what attributes runs to a prize. _(unsorry-side change; PR held.)_

4. **Domain context → URL-prefixed, new top axis.** A site-wide header **domain selector** implemented as a **URL prefix** (`/math/...`), a **new top-level axis above** guild-hall's categories (categories become sub-filters within a domain). It filters leaderboard, showcase, proof graph, queue, prizes, and profiles. Ship the dropdown now with **Math as the only option**; per-tier (`SCORED`/`CONSENSUS`) UI is deferred until a second domain exists. This is the UI seam for ADR-030. The **domain registry is a PR-reviewed file in the unsorry repo** (git, ADR-030-aligned), read by the guild like any other artifact; unsorry's **generators stamp a `domain` field** on each record (constant `math` today) so the ported pages can filter. _(unsorry-side; PRs held.)_

5. **The four pages → reimplement as Next pages.** Rebuild **leaderboard, showcase, proof graph, queue** as React/Next pages, inheriting the header, domain selector, dark theme, and nav rather than being bolted on. **Sourcing per surface (refined per [maintainer note](https://github.com/agenticsnz/unsorry-guild/issues/1#issuecomment-4760688846)):**
   - **Leaderboard + profiles' global standing are Decision-#2 surfaces — recompute from the raw git records on read** (`library/index/*.aisp`, `goals/*.aisp`/`goal_effort`, `proof-runs/*.aisp`), which the proof-merge PRs commit in real time. This structurally removes any GitHub-Actions/cron lag in the derived `leaderboard-ui.json`. The baked `leaderboard-ui.json` is only a **stopgap** (now near-real-time again via unsorry#3735, push-on-merge + cron backstop). *(Per-target leaderboards already recompute from `library/index` — consistent.)*
   - **Showcase / proof graph / queue** consume the generated artifacts (`showcase.html`, `proof-graph.svg`, `docs/queue.json`) — generators stay in unsorry.
   - **Timeline caveat:** the proofs-over-time series (`timelines.merge` / `timelines.solve`, cumulative hourly buckets from commit history) is too heavy to recompute per request — keep a periodically-built cache for that series even in the recompute-on-read model (see Open items).

6. **Theme → dark default, keep the toggle.** Dark is the default (`src/app/layout.tsx` → `defaultTheme="dark"`); the `light` / `warm` options stay.

7. **Repo strategy → hard fork, prune later.** Fully diverge from guild-hall. Disable dead surface (auth/email/quest-lifecycle) behind flags now to ship fast; **aggressive prune + migration squash after the first vertical slice validates the model** (see Suggested first slice). We won't track upstream guild-hall.

8. **Hosting → guild on its own subdomain.** Deploy `unsorry-guild` to **Netlify at `swarm.unsorry.agentics.org.nz`**; unsorry's existing pages stay at `unsorry.agentics.org.nz`. The two sites **coexist** — no DNS cutover or Pages retirement now (revisit later if desired). unsorry's generators keep emitting the JSON artifacts the guild reads either way.

## Open items

Design direction is settled. What remains is implementation detail (for the plan stage) and cross-repo work in unsorry (PRs **held** until the plan is approved — see the PR-hold note).

**Deferred to the plan stage (implementation detail):**
- Overlay table schema (`prizes`, `criteria`, `targets`, `awards`/frozen-season-results, admin content) and the recompute-on-read **cache TTL**.
- Exact derivation of a target's **dependency / sub-lemma tree** from `goals/*.aisp` `deps` (what counts toward a prize, and toward the progress indicator).
- Per-tier (`SCORED` / `CONSENSUS`) UI — deferred until a second domain exists.
- **Recompute-on-read leaderboard fidelity** (Decision #5): the live recompute must faithfully reproduce the official score components — `dispatch_points`, contributor-alias merging (`contributor-aliases.json`), and inferred-git-author proofs — or it diverges from unsorry's board. Until that's ported, the baked `leaderboard-ui.json` (fresh via unsorry#3735) remains the source; the recompute path is the structural target.
- **Timeline-series cache** (Decision #5 caveat): keep a periodically-built cache for `timelines.merge`/`timelines.solve` rather than scanning commit history on each request.

**Cross-repo work in unsorry (PRs on hold):**
1. **Target-awareness in the swarm CLI** — extend the existing `--goal <id>` (in `swarm/run.sh`, `agent.sh`) to a `--target <id>` across `run.sh` / `agent.sh` / `sourcing.sh`, so runs attribute to a flagship target. *(drives Decision #3)*
2. **Domain registry file** (git, PR-reviewed) in unsorry. *(Decision #4)*
3. **Stamp a `domain` field** on the generated artifacts (`leaderboard` / `visualiser` / `queue_board`). *(Decision #4)*
4. *(future)* Promote the **ADR-035 triviality battery from advisory to a blocking gate** (the "blocking triviality gate").
5. *(future)* A **goal / target issue template** extending `propose-goal.md` / `propose-target.md`.
6. *(future)* The **ADR-078 `targets/` registry** as the eventual backing for prizes (today: `goals/*.aisp` + difficulty).

## Suggested first slice

A thin vertical to de-risk the model before the big build:
1. **Theme + auth (#6, #1)** — dark default; rip out login/registration/email; reduce to public read-only + a single admin.
2. **Read-only leaderboard + profiles** sourced from unsorry's existing `docs/metrics/leaderboard-ui.json`, keyed on GitHub handle (proves the git-as-source path).
3. **One hardcoded "Math" domain** wired as a URL-prefixed header context that filters that leaderboard (proves the ADR-030 seam).
4. **One flagship-target prize** end-to-end — a target (goal id + dependency tree), its per-prize seasoned leaderboard, a live progress indicator, and podium + contributor badges on profiles (proves the novel mechanic).

## Appendix — unsorry integration reference (facts the build depends on)

Concrete unsorry-side facts the `unsorry-guild` build relies on, captured here so this issue is self-contained.

### A. Data artifacts the guild reads (git-native, generated by unsorry CI)
All live under unsorry's `docs/`, regenerated by GitHub Actions and committed to `main`:

| Artifact | Generator / workflow | Cadence | Feeds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docs/metrics/leaderboard-ui.json` (+ `community-stats.json`, `attribution-gaps.json`, `sourcing-leaderboard.json`) | `tools/leaderboard` / `leaderboard.yml` | **on merge (push); cron backstop** (unsorry#3735 — previously cron-only `*/10`, throttled to ~1/h) | Leaderboard + profiles (stopgap — see Decision #5) |
| `docs/proof-graph.svg`, `docs/proofs-contributors-visualisation.html` | `tools/visualiser` / `proofs-visualisation.yml` | on push to `main` | Proof graph |
| `docs/queue.html`, `docs/queue.json` | `tools/queue_board` / `queue-board.yml` | ~15 min | Queue |
| `docs/showcase.html` | hand-authored | manual | Showcase |

Leaderboard contributor record shape (`leaderboard-ui.json`):
```
{ github, display_name ("@handle"), avatar_url, rank, score,
  difficulty_points, credited_proofs, attempt_yield,
  badges: { difficulty, proofs, success_rate_percent },
  credit_sources: ["explicit-solver", "inferred-git-add-author"] }
```
The **board score is precomputed** in the artifact: `score = difficulty_points*100 + credited_proofs*25` (rank 1 today: 1688×100 + 811×25 = 189,075). The guild can consume `score`/`rank` directly, or recompute per-prize from the same fields. **Identity key = `github` handle** (matches Decision #1). This file is the natural source for the first-slice leaderboard + profiles.

### B. Hosting today (relevant to the Decision #5 cutover)
- unsorry Pages: **legacy Jekyll**, served from **`main:/`** (docs/ served at the site root), custom domain **`unsorry.agentics.org.nz`**, HTTPS enforced. **No Pages deploy workflow** — Pages auto-rebuilds whenever a generator commits to `main`.
- Generators push straight to `main` with a `REFRESH_TOKEN` admin PAT + `[skip ci]`, bypassing branch protection.
- Retiring/redirecting = stop the doc-commits and repoint the CNAME / add redirects; there is no workflow to disable.

### C. Goal authoring today (relevant to Decision #3 prize-criterion vocabulary)
- Issue templates already exist: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/propose-goal.md` and `propose-target.md` (classic markdown + frontmatter; sections: summary, skeleton, "already established", non-triviality, absence from mathlib, difficulty/scope). A guild "goal/prize template" should **extend these, not reinvent them**.
- A goal is an AISP record (`Skills/unsorry-goal-sourcing/assets/goal-record.aisp.tmpl`): fields `id, phase, status (open/proved/archived), difficulty (1–5), src (backlog/*.md), deps, lean (goals/*.lean), sha, aff (affinity)`, plus a Lean statement file.
- unsorry's swarm CLI already supports targeting: `swarm/run.sh` and `swarm/agent.sh` accept `--goal <id>` (restrict/override selection to one goal); `swarm/sourcing.sh` is theme/pool-driven (no `--goal`). The flagship-target plumbing (Decision #3) extends this to a `--target <id>` across all three.
- **ADR-078's `targets/` registry does not exist yet** — sponsor-registered targets are *proposed only*. So "model a prize on an ADR-078 target" is forward-looking; **today a prize must be defined against `goals/*.aisp` + difficulty**.

### D. Credit & anti-farm mechanics (the substrate under Decision #3)
- **Board score basis** = ADR-023 (`difficulty_points` + `credited_proofs`), being reformed by ADR-078 (credited obligations) — see the top callout.
- **ADR-035 triviality battery** (Status: **Accepted**): tactics `rfl | trivial | decide | norm_num | omega | simp | simp_all | aesop | ring | linarith | tauto`; deliberately **excludes** `nlinarith | positivity | field_simp | gcongr` (reserved for ADR-078 registration probes). Tool: `tools/sourcing/check_triviality.py`.
- It is **advisory at merge today**: `.github/workflows/triviality.yml` posts a sticky comment and **always exits 0** — explicitly *not* a required check; the real block is **at sourcing admission (a human step)**. The "blocking triviality gate" idea is *promoting this to a blocking gate* (future, on hold).
- **Required status checks on `main`** (branch protection): **`gate-a`** (soundness — kernel re-verify, axiom audit, statement binding) and **`gate-b`**. Triviality is *not* among them.
- **ADR-078 and ADR-079 are both Status: Proposed (2026-06-20)**; their SPEC files aren't in the tree yet. The credit reform is *direction*, not yet shipped.

**Priority: High.** Found in the functional+wiring audit (#2).

**Gap:** four disconnected notions of value — Coins (earned on votes but **never displayed**), `rep` (drives profile `cityRank`), a `challenges*5 + votes_given` **formula** (drives the leaderboard + pool-share %), and `usd/inr` cash (never credited). # Feature: Off Grid Play

## Purpose

Off Grid Play allows players to enjoy the full Gr8Day Bingo experience without providing an email address.

This feature is designed for players who value their privacy, do not use email, or simply prefer not to share an email address. It removes a common barrier to participation while keeping the registration process simple.

Off Grid Play is intended to encourage participation, not discourage it.

---

# Registration

During registration, players choose one of two account types.

## Standard Account

* Email address required
* Password required
* Eligible for prize draws
* Supports email-based password recovery

## Off Grid Play

* No email address required
* Username required
* Password required
* Not eligible for prize draws
* Full access to all other game features

---

# Off Grid Play Information

A **Help ( ? )** icon shall appear beside the **Off Grid Play** option during registration.

Selecting the Help icon displays the following message:

## What is Off Grid Play?

Off Grid Play lets you enjoy Gr8Day Bingo without providing an email address.

You can:

* Play Gr8Day Bingo
* Complete and record deeds
* Earn Bingos
* Join teams
* Participate on leaderboards
* Advance through player levels
* Enjoy all normal game features

The trade-offs are:

* You are **not eligible for prize draws.**
* If you forget your username or password, we **may not be able to recover your account.**

You may add an email address later and convert your account to a Standard Account to become eligible for future prize draws.

---

# Player Capabilities

Off Grid players have access to the same gameplay features as Standard players.

They can:

* Receive bingo cards
* Complete deeds
* Record deeds
* Earn Bingos
* Participate in challenges
* Join teams
* Participate in team activities
* Earn player levels
* Appear on leaderboards
* View statistics
* Use all future player features unless specifically restricted

The only gameplay restriction is prize eligibility.

---

# Prize Eligibility

Off Grid players are **not eligible** for any prize draws.

If an Off Grid player later converts to a Standard Account, they become eligible for future prize draws only.

Previous prize draws are not affected.

---

# Login

Off Grid players log in using:

* Username
* Password

Email is never required.

---

# Password Recovery

Because Off Grid Play does not require an email address, automated password recovery is not available.

During registration, before the account is created, the player must acknowledge the following statement:

> "I understand that because I have chosen Off Grid Play without providing an email address, we may not be able to recover my account if I forget my username or password."

Registration cannot continue until this acknowledgement has been accepted.

---

# Administrative Assistance

Account recovery for Off Grid players is provided on a best-effort basis only.

If an Off Grid player forgets their username or password:

* The admin may assist if the player's identity can be reasonably verified.
* Recovery is not guaranteed.
* If ownership cannot be confidently verified, the admin may require the player to create a new account.

This policy protects both player privacy and account security.

---

# Admin Features

The admin shall be able to:

* Search for Off Grid players
* View username
* Reset password
* Change username if required
* Convert an Off Grid account into a Standard Account
* Add or update an email address
* Enable prize eligibility after conversion

---

# Converting to a Standard Account

An Off Grid player may convert to a Standard Account at any time.

To convert:

* Add a valid email address.
* Verify the email address if email verification is enabled.
* The account type changes from Off Grid to Standard.
* The player becomes eligible for all future prize draws.

No gameplay history, deeds, Bingos, teams, or statistics are lost during conversion.

---

# Database Requirements

Support the following account types:

* Standard
* Off Grid

Email shall be optional for Off Grid accounts.

Suggested fields include:

* Account Type
* Username
* Password Hash
* Email (nullable)
* Prize Eligible
* Date Converted (optional)

---

# Acceptance Criteria

* Players can register without providing an email address.
* Players can choose either Standard or Off Grid Play during registration.
* A Help ( ? ) icon explains Off Grid Play before the player registers.
* Off Grid players can participate in all normal gameplay except prize draws.
* Off Grid players log in using username and password.
* Email-based password recovery is not available for Off Grid accounts.
* Players must acknowledge the recovery limitation before creating an Off Grid account.
* Admin may assist with account recovery on a best-effort basis.
* Admin can convert an Off Grid account into a Standard Account.
* Existing Standard Account functionality remains unchanged.

## Summary

The Cloud Quest gamified-event MVP is **feature-complete**: a multi-event platform where an **admin** builds events (map, stands, activities, badges, prizes, staff), **participants** register + show a unique QR, and **staff** scan players at their stand to award points server-side. Built as **20 squash-merged PRs (#1–#20)** across three sub-projects, every slice with a fresh adversarial review. All acceptance criteria **CA-01 … CA-10** are met, and the core flow was **verified live end-to-end** (browser + DB).

Authoritative spec: `docs/specs/2026-06-21-mvp-scope-reconciled.md`. Live schema: `supabase/migrations/0001–0009` (`supabase/schema.sql` is DEPRECATED).

---

## ⚠️ Required setup before testing

1. **Disable email confirmation** in Supabase → Authentication → Sign In / Providers → Email → turn **OFF** "Confirm email". Otherwise registration shows "Revisa tu email" and never logs in.
2. Use **real email domains** for test accounts (`@gmail.com` etc.) — GoTrue rejects `@example.com`.
3. `.env.local` needs `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` (server-only), `ADMIN_EMAILS` (server-only). Run `npm run seed:admin` to populate the admin allowlist.
4. Current DB is **`stan_aws`** (dev/test). A **separate Supabase project + Vercel deploy** is recommended for the real event.

```bash
npm install && npm run dev   # http://localhost:3000
```

---

## How to test (per role)

- **Participant:** "Comenzar" → register (name + real email + password) → map (DB stands) → open a stand (read-only, "show QR to staff") → "Mostrar mi código QR" → Ranking.
- **Admin:** register with an email in `ADMIN_EMAILS` → "Panel del organizador" / `/admin` → create/edit events, stands (+ visual map editor), activities, badges, prizes; create staff & manage participant accounts; correct points; validate winners.
- **Staff:** admin creates + assigns them to a stand → they log in (→ `/staff`) → pick station → scan a participant's QR (or enter the code manually) → player is credited.

---

## Review / QA checklist

**SP1 — Foundation (#1–5)**
- [ ] Signup creates a profile; allowlisted email → `admin`; catalog loads from DB; per-event progress via `participations`; auto-join single active event.

**SP2 — Admin (#6–9, #18)**
- [ ] CA-10: create/edit event, stands (map editor place/drag), activities, badges, prizes.
- [ ] CA-09: admin creates staff accounts + assigns; lists/edits/deletes participant accounts. Non-admin blocked (RLS + route guard).

**SP3 — Staff scan & scoring (#10–17, #19)**
- [ ] CA-03/04: staff scans QR → +points/badge/piece once; re-scan → "Ya participó" (no double credit).
- [ ] CA-06: leaderboard ranks by points. CA-07: point corrections with audit history. CA-08: winner validation by QR (top-3 / all-badges). Prize claim deducts tickets + stock server-side.
- [ ] Integrity: all scoring/claiming is server-side (SECURITY DEFINER RPCs); a direct client \`update participations set tickets=9999\` is **rejected** (grant revoked).

**Cross-cutting**
- [ ] Realtime: player screen updates live after a staff scan. Redirects by role. Neutral-Spanish copy. `npm test` per-file green (~95 integration tests against live Supabase).

---

## Known non-blocking findings (from the live E2E)

- **Setup:** email confirmation is currently ON in `stan_aws` (see Required setup #1).
- **Test infra:** running the full suite at once trips Supabase auth's signup rate limit — run per-file (`npx vitest run test/<file>`).
- **Security (LOW):** TOCTOU window on participant delete; no Next-layer rate limit on admin endpoints (platform-inherent).
- **Schema:** `completions.approved_by` has no `on delete cascade` → deleting a staff member who approved completions is blocked (audit guard; fine in practice since CA-09 delete is participant-scoped).
- Both UI findings surfaced by the E2E (map per-stand count showing `/3`, leaderboard `VOS` voseo) were **already fixed** in #20.

## Idea

Host scheduled virtual stair-stepper race events where users sign up in advance, race the same climb at a synchronized start time, see live leaderboard positions, and earn prizes for top finishers.

Inspired by [Tower Running](https://www.towerrunning.com/races/) — the existing real-world community of organized stair-climbing races (Empire State Building Run-Up, ICC Sears Tower, etc.). Ascend's version: same competitive event format, but you don't have to travel.

## Why it fits Ascend's positioning

- Natural extension of Live Climbs — same race mechanic, live participants instead of replay ghosts
- Reaches the tower-running-curious audience who can't travel for physical events (geography, cost, time)
- Recurring events drive retention better than push notifications — people pre-register and clear their calendar around the event
- Aligns with the "leaderboard is the conversation" framing

## Already supported (no net-new work)

- Headphone-motion live tracking
- Per-attempt replay leaderboards
- Climb catalog with real landmarks
- Bucketed split math for elapsed-time rank comparison

## Net-new work required

- Event scheduling + pre-registration UI
- Synchronized start countdown across all participants
- Live multi-user broadcast layer (vs. polling published replay rows)
- **Anti-cheat for prizes** — likely combining headphone motion + Apple Health HR + a verification window for podium finishers. Solvable, but non-trivial. This is the spicy one.
- Prize fulfillment (digital badges/avatars first; physical merch or cash later as scale supports it)

## Architectural note for now

The current `live_replay_leaderboards` data model and per-climb replay contexts should stay flexible enough to accommodate synchronized real-time entries later — not just published replays of already-completed attempts. Don't paint into a corner where every replay row is keyed to a single completed workout ID.

## Roadmap placement

v2+ — after core Live Climbs is polished and the user base is large enough to fill an event roster (rough threshold: ~50+ active climbers per landmark per event window).

**FEATURE DESCRIPTION**

# Weekly Prize Entries

## Purpose

Every completed Gr8Day Deed deserves recognition.

While earning a bingo is exciting, the real purpose of Gr8Day Bingo is to inspire people to make a positive difference every day. The Weekly Prize Draw rewards players for every completed Gr8Day Deed, encouraging consistent participation throughout the week.

---

## How It Works

Every time a player successfully completes and confirms a Gr8Day Deed, they automatically receive one entry into the Weekly Prize Draw.

Each completed deed equals one prize entry.

Examples:

* Complete 1 deed = 1 entry
* Complete 8 deeds = 8 entries
* Complete 25 deeds = 25 entries

The more Gr8Day Deeds a player completes during the week, the more chances they have to win.

---

## Weekly Draw

All prize entries earned during the current game week are automatically entered into that week's prize draw.

At the end of the week:

* One or more winners are randomly selected.
* All weekly entries are cleared.
* Everyone starts the new week with zero entries.

Every week is a fresh opportunity for every player.

---

## Eligibility

A Weekly Prize Entry is awarded only after:

* The Gr8Day Deed has been completed.
* The player confirms completion.
* Any required verification has been satisfied (if applicable).

Simply revealing a bingo square or selecting a deed does not earn an entry.

Only completed Gr8Day Deeds qualify.

---

## Fair Play

The system monitors participation for unusual activity. Entries that appear inconsistent with normal play may be flagged for administrative review.

The goal is to reward genuine acts of kindness while maintaining fairness for all players.

---

## Administrative Settings

The administrator can configure:

* Enable or disable the Weekly Prize Draw.
* Number of weekly winners.
* Prize descriptions and values.
* Entries awarded per completed deed.
* Maximum entries per player per week (optional).
* Winner eligibility rules.
* Draw day and time.
* Winner notification method.
* Historical winner reporting.

---

## Player Dashboard

Players can view:

* Gr8Day Deeds completed this week.
* Weekly prize entries earned.
* Lifetime prize entries earned.
* Lifetime prizes won.
* Previous weekly winners.

---

## Design Goal

The Weekly Prize Draw reinforces the true purpose of Gr8Day Bingo: creating more positive moments in the world.

Every completed Gr8Day Deed earns another chance to win, because every act of kindness counts.

**SAMPLE CLAUDE CODE**

Implement a new Weekly Draw Entry system for HavaGr8Day Bingo.

CURRENT SYSTEM CONTEXT

The game currently awards weekly prize draw eligibility based mainly on completed bingos.

This needs to change.

NEW FEATURE INTENTION

The purpose of this feature is to reward every completed Gr8Day deed, not just completed bingos.

The intended behaviour is:

Every deed matters.

Players should feel that even if they do not complete a bingo, their good deeds still count toward the weekly prize draw.

Bingos should still be rewarded, but as a bonus rather than the only way to earn draw entries.

CORE RULES

1. Every completed deed earns draw entries immediately.

Default:

* 1 completed deed = 1 draw entry

This applies to:

* Bingo card deeds
* Quick Tap deeds
* Repeated deeds
* Any future deed source, as long as the deed is recorded as completed

If a player completes the same deed multiple times, each completed occurrence earns another draw entry.

2. Every completed bingo earns bonus draw entries.

The number of bonus entries per bingo must be controlled by an admin setting.

The bonus applies to every bingo completed, not just the first bingo of the week.

Example:

* Admin setting: Bingo Bonus Entries = 10
* Player completes 3 bingos
* Player earns 30 bonus draw entries

3. Draw entries are awarded immediately.

When a deed is marked completed, the system should immediately:

* Record the completed deed
* Award the deed draw entry
* Update the player’s active draw entry balance
* Check whether the deed completed any bingo
* If bingo is completed, award the admin-configured bingo bonus entries immediately

Do not wait until the weekly draw to calculate entries.

4. Use balances, not physical ticket records.

Do not create millions of individual ticket rows.

Use player draw entry balances instead.

Track at minimum:

* Active Draw Entries
* Lifetime Draw Entries Earned
* This Week’s Draw Entries
* Last Draw Win Date
* Last Participation Date
* Last Entry Earned Date

The weekly draw should select a winner using weighted random selection based on Active Draw Entries.

Players do not see ticket totals or draw mechanics unless admin later chooses to expose them.

Player-facing message should simply be:
“Congratulations! You won this week’s Gr8Day Draw!”

5. Ticket rollover rules

Draw entries roll over from week to week if the player continues participating.

A player must participate in the current week to be eligible for that week’s draw.

Participation means completing at least one deed during the current weekly game period.

If a player does not participate that week, their accumulated draw entries do not qualify for that week’s draw.

6. Inactive player expiration

Add an admin-controlled inactivity expiration setting.

Admin options should include:

* Never Expire
* 1 Week
* 2 Weeks
* 4 Weeks
* 8 Weeks
* 12 Weeks
* Custom Number of Weeks

If a player exceeds the configured inactivity period, reset Active Draw Entries to zero.

Do not reset Lifetime Draw Entries Earned.

7. Winner reset rule

When a player wins the weekly draw:

* Reset that player’s Active Draw Entries to zero
* Keep Lifetime Draw Entries Earned unchanged
* Record the win date
* Record the winning draw event
* Record the reset in the audit trail

8. Reversed or invalid deeds

If an admin reverses or removes a completed deed:

* Automatically remove the draw entry originally awarded for that deed
* If reversing that deed also removes a bingo, remove the related bingo bonus entries
* Update the player’s active balance
* Update this week’s balance if applicable
* Record everything in the audit trail

Draw entries should not remain if the qualifying deed or bingo no longer qualifies.

ADMIN SETTINGS

Add a Weekly Draw settings section with:

* Enable Weekly Draw: Yes/No
* Enable Deed Draw Entries: Yes/No
* Draw Entries per Deed: default 1
* Enable Bingo Bonus Entries: Yes/No
* Bingo Bonus Entries per Bingo: admin-defined
* Include Quick Tap Deeds: Yes/No
* Allow Ticket Rollovers: Yes/No
* Require Current Week Participation: Yes/No
* Reset Active Entries After Win: Yes/No
* Inactive Entry Expiration: Never / 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 12 / Custom weeks

Defaults:

* Enable Weekly Draw: Yes
* Enable Deed Draw Entries: Yes
* Draw Entries per Deed: 1
* Enable Bingo Bonus Entries: Yes
* Include Quick Tap Deeds: Yes
* Allow Ticket Rollovers: Yes
* Require Current Week Participation: Yes
* Reset Active Entries After Win: Yes
* Inactive Entry Expiration: Custom or configurable

LEADERBOARD / ADMIN REPORTING

Add individual player draw entry data to the existing leaderboard.

Individual only.

Do not add team draw entries because there are currently no team prizes beyond bragging rights.

Admin leaderboard fields should include:

* Player Name
* This Week’s Draw Entries
* Active Draw Entries
* Lifetime Draw Entries Earned
* Last Draw Win
* Last Participation Date
* Current Week Eligible: Yes/No

AUDIT TRAIL

Audit trail must record everything.

Track:

* Deed entry awarded
* Quick Tap entry awarded
* Bingo bonus entries awarded
* Entry removed due to reversed deed
* Bingo bonus removed due to bingo reversal
* Manual admin adjustment
* Weekly draw winner selected
* Winner active entries reset
* Inactive player entries expired
* Setting changes

Each audit record should include:

* Player ID
* Admin ID if applicable
* Source event
* Entry amount added or removed
* Previous balance
* New balance
* Timestamp
* Reason
* Related deed ID if applicable
* Related bingo ID if applicable
* Related draw ID if applicable

DRAW LOGIC

When running the weekly draw:

1. Confirm Weekly Draw is enabled.
2. Identify players who are eligible.
3. A player is eligible if:

   * They have Active Draw Entries greater than zero
   * They completed at least one deed during the current weekly game period if current week participation is required
   * Their entries have not expired due to inactivity
4. Use weighted random selection based on Active Draw Entries.
5. Record the selected winner.
6. Reset winner’s Active Draw Entries to zero if the admin setting is enabled.
7. Record all actions in audit trail.
8. Notify or mark winner using the existing prize winner flow.

PLAYER EXPERIENCE

Do not show players complex draw mechanics.

Do not show:

* Exact ticket count
* Weighted odds
* Audit records
* Other players’ entries

Player only needs to know they won if selected.

TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS

Before coding:

* Review the current database schema
* Identify existing deed completion records
* Identify existing bingo completion logic
* Identify existing prize draw logic
* Identify existing leaderboard structure
* Identify existing admin settings structure
* Reuse existing patterns wherever possible

Implementation must:

* Avoid duplicate draw entry awards for the same completed deed event
* Avoid duplicate bingo bonus awards for the same bingo event
* Be idempotent
* Be safe if the same deed completion event is processed twice
* Support future deed sources
* Include validation and error handling
* Include migration scripts if needed
* Include tests for all core rules

TEST CASES TO INCLUDE

1. Player completes one bingo card deed.
   Expected: 1 active draw entry awarded.

2. Player completes one Quick Tap deed.
   Expected: 1 active draw entry awarded.

3. Player completes same deed 5 times.
   Expected: 5 draw entries awarded.

4. Player completes a bingo.
   Expected: deed entry plus bingo bonus entries awarded.

5. Player completes multiple bingos.
   Expected: bonus awarded for each bingo.

6. Player does not win weekly draw.
   Expected: active entries roll over.

7. Player wins weekly draw.
   Expected: active entries reset to zero, lifetime entries remain unchanged.

8. Player skips a week.
   Expected: entries are inactive for draw if current week participation is required.

9. Player exceeds inactivity expiration setting.
   Expected: active entries reset to zero.

10. Admin reverses deed.
    Expected: related draw entry removed.

11. Admin reverses deed that caused bingo.
    Expected: deed entry and bingo bonus entries removed.

12. Weekly draw disabled.
    Expected: no draw is run.

13. Deed draw entries disabled.
    Expected: deeds do not create draw entries.

14. Bingo bonus disabled.
    Expected: bingo does not create bonus entries.

15. Duplicate event processing.
    Expected: no duplicate draw entries awarded.

DELIVERABLES

Please provide:

1. Database changes required
2. Backend service logic
3. Admin settings changes
4. Leaderboard changes
5. Weekly draw logic
6. Audit trail implementation
7. Reversal logic
8. Tests
9. Any risks or edge cases found in the current codebase
10. A short implementation summary after completion

A web-researched completeness audit of mechanism families to check against `docs/landscape.html` (and the broader catalog). This is a **diff-list to verify** — presence/absence on the current page is not certified here, so each item should be checked before adding. The landscape today is organized around scoring/parimutuel/prediction-market/chaining structures; several large mechanism-design families below are candidates it may not yet cover.

### Must-not-miss (strongest additions first)
- [ ] Peer prediction / Bayesian Truth Serum / Correlated Agreement / DMI / Mutual Information Paradigm
- [ ] Scoring-rule markets for arbitrary elicitable statistics
- [ ] Incentive-compatible forecasting competitions (winner-take-all does **not** preserve affine proper-score incentives)
- [ ] Decision markets and futarchy
- [ ] CFMMs / AMMs as cost-function prediction-market cousins (concave-potential CFMM ≈ cost-function market; implies a proper scoring rule)
- [ ] Quadratic funding and (dominant) assurance contracts
- [ ] Deferred acceptance, TTC, probabilistic serial, matching with contracts
- [ ] GSP / GFP sponsored-search auctions
- [ ] Budget-feasible procurement and data-acquisition mechanisms
- [ ] Sample elicitation and kernel / MMD scoring rules

### 1. Scoring-rule & elicitation mechanisms
- [ ] Log score / logarithmic market scoring rule family; Quadratic/Brier; spherical & pseudospherical; CRPS; pinball/quantile; expectile; interval/Winkler; Dawid–Sebastiani; Hyvärinen; energy; variogram; kernel/MMD scores
- [ ] Weighted, censored, threshold-weighted, tail-focused scores
- [ ] Joint elicitability: VaR + Expected Shortfall, Range VaR, multi-functional reports
- [ ] Set-valued elicitation: prediction intervals, quantile sets, Vorob'ev quantiles
- [ ] Murphy-diagram / elementary-score decompositions
- [ ] Sample elicitation (reward submitted samples, not densities); elicit estimate + confidence/sample count

### 2. Prediction-market mechanisms
- [ ] LMSR; market scoring rules generally; cost-function & convex cost-function markets; securities-based markets; scoring-rule markets for arbitrary elicitable statistics
- [ ] Share-ratio / ratio-of-expectations markets
- [ ] Dynamic parimutuel market (Pennock); sequential convex parimutuel (SCPM); dynamic parimutuel information markets; interval-security markets for continuous outcomes
- [ ] Liquidity-sensitive LMSR; no-regret-learning interpretation of market makers
- [ ] Conditional prediction markets; futarchy; decision markets; proxy decision markets; Policy Analysis Market / FutureMAP (historical)

### 3. Forecasting competitions & wager mechanisms
- [ ] Winner-take-all contests; proper-score prize contests; incentive-compatible competitions; randomized prize mechanisms
- [ ] Arbitrage-resistant & collusion-resistant scoring; non-myopic incentives
- [ ] Stake-weighted proper-score wagers; peer-comparative rewards; budget-balanced scoring contests; rank/prize-transform tournaments

### 4. Peer prediction / information without verification
- [ ] Classic peer prediction; Bayesian Truth Serum; Robust BTS; Dasgupta–Ghosh; Correlated Agreement; Output Agreement; Peer Truth Serum
- [ ] Determinant Mutual Information (DMI); Volume Mutual Information (VMI); Mutual Information Paradigm
- [ ] Peer prediction with effort elicitation; sequential posted-price peer prediction; proxy forecasting; truth discovery + incentives; crowdsourced judgment with unknown skill

### 5. Automated market makers / DeFi-adjacent
- [ ] Constant-product / constant-sum / constant-mean (Balancer) / stable-swap (Curve); general CFMMs; concave-potential CFMMs
- [ ] CFMMs as prediction-market analogues; replicating market makers for derivatives; AMM price oracles
- [ ] Myersonian optimal liquidity provision; bid–ask spread under adverse selection; Maniswap / Manifold AMM (example)

### 6. Auction mechanisms
- [ ] English / Dutch / first-price / Vickrey (second-price); VCG; Clarke pivot; GSP / GFP sponsored-search; quality-adjusted ad auctions
- [ ] Uniform-price / discriminatory; all-pay; war-of-attrition
- [ ] Myerson optimal; reserve prices; ironed virtual values; Bayesian-optimal; prior-independent; prior-free; RSEM; profit-extraction; consensus-estimate
- [ ] Budget-feasible procurement; deferred-acceptance auctions; combinatorial / package / core-selecting / combinatorial-clock; double auctions (McAfee, continuous, call); procurement scoring & multiattribute auctions; truthful scheduling; learned/neural auctions

### 7. Matching & assignment
- [ ] Gale–Shapley deferred acceptance (student/school-proposing); school choice; Boston & adaptive Boston; TTC / TTCC; serial dictatorship; random serial dictatorship / random priority; probabilistic serial
- [ ] House allocation; kidney-exchange cycles & chains; stable matching with contracts; Hatfield–Milgrom cumulative offer; hospital–residents; matching with couples; cadet-branch; assignment-game

### 8. Voting & social choice
- [ ] Plurality; approval; score/range; Borda; Condorcet; IRV; STV; median-voter; generalized median with phantom voters; strategyproof single-peaked
- [ ] Quadratic voting; liquid democracy; participatory budgeting; random dictatorship; sortition
- [ ] Boundaries: Gibbard–Satterthwaite; Arrow impossibility

### 9. Public goods & collective funding
- [ ] Lindahl pricing; Clarke/Groves; VCG public-project; provision-point; assurance & dominant assurance contracts
- [ ] Quadratic funding (capital-constrained, connection-oriented); matching funds; Gitcoin grants (example)
- [ ] Harberger tax / COST; land-value / Georgist (if broad enough); curation markets; token-curated registries

### 10. Fair division
- [ ] Divide-and-choose; last diminisher; Even–Paz; Dubins–Spanier & Stromquist moving-knife; Selfridge–Conway; Robertson–Webb query model; online cake-cutting (Fink); randomized partial-proportional
- [ ] EF1; EFX; maximin share (MMS); Nash social welfare; CEEI

### 11. Contest, prize & crowdsourcing
- [ ] Rank-order tournaments; all-pay contests; Tullock contests; innovation prizes; Kaggle-style leaderboards; crowdsourcing contests
- [ ] Optimal prize splits; multiple-prize design; effort-eliciting; social-network invitation contests; referral & bounty mechanisms; hackathon judging

### 12. Data / ML / federated-learning incentives
- [ ] Data-procurement auctions; budget-feasible data acquisition; truthful crowdsourced labeling; peer-prediction labeling
- [ ] Federated-learning participation incentives & contribution pricing; Shapley-value payments; contract-theoretic & Stackelberg FL; blockchain-enforced model/data exchange; federated prediction-serving; truthful local-model reporting

---

_Note:_ many of these are outside the page's current remit (scoring / parimutuel / chained probabilistic elicitation). A decision is needed on scope: keep the landscape focused on **prediction/scoring/chaining** mechanisms (in which case §1–5, §11–12 are the relevant additions and the rest are out of scope), or broaden it to a general **mechanism-design** landscape (in which case §6–10 belong too, likely as a separate page or section). Recommend triaging the must-not-miss list first.
title: Landscape / catalog completeness audit: mechanism families to check & triage

## Description

Several components do not adapt to mobile screen sizes, causing horizontal overflow and broken layouts.

## Issues

### TournamentLeaderboard (V2)
The table header and rows use a hard-coded 5-column CSS grid with fixed pixel widths (`grid-cols-[60px_1fr_140px_100px_120px]`). The fixed columns alone sum to 420px, which overflows on phones (~375px wide). There are no responsive breakpoints on this grid at all.

### LeaderboardHeader
The header is a single `flex-row justify-between` with no wrapping, so the tournament title/info and prize amount are forced side by side on any screen width, squeezing both.

### RecentEvent — winner username overflow
The right-side flex column has no width constraint, so `truncate` has nothing to truncate against. **On mobile, the winning username overflows its container and only the country flag is shown.** ⚠️ **This behaviour (truncating to flag-only on very small screens) should be confirmed with Obi before merging**, as it may be intentional or may require a different treatment (e.g. a tooltip or different layout).

body:
## The Risk

Apple's App Store guideline 4.2 (Minimum Functionality) requires that an app include features that "elevate it beyond a repackaged website" and is "not primarily... a collection of links." Apple reviewers specifically reject multi-game apps that feel like a container rather than a product — one where the games could just as easily have been separate apps or a website.

**BC Arcade currently has:**
- 12 games (6 free, 6 premium via entitlement JWT)
- Per-game leaderboards (most without even a dedicated UI screen)
- A profile showing total games, favorite game, top score, games tried
- No cross-game XP, currency, levels, or achievements
- No daily challenge system spanning multiple games
- Session-anonymous (no account/sign-in)

Profiles and leaderboards alone are not sufficient. Research across approved multi-game apps (Microsoft Solitaire Collection, GAMEE Prizes, Daily Pastimes) shows Apple reviewers look for **functional evidence** that the collection is one product — specifically: a shared economy, a daily hook that opens the *app* rather than a specific game, and at least one feature that couldn't exist on a website.

---

## What Approved Multi-Game Apps All Have

| Feature | Microsoft Solitaire | GAMEE Prizes | Daily Pastimes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shared currency/points | ✅ unified coins + XP | ✅ tickets | ✅ diamond ranking |
| Daily cross-game challenge | ✅ spans all 5 variants | ✅ tournaments | ✅ timed daily rounds |
| Unified leaderboard | ✅ Game Center | ✅ global | ✅ cross-game |
| Seasonal events | ✅ platform-wide | ✅ prize draws | — |
| Native OS integration | ✅ Game Center, Xbox | ✅ Game Center | ✅ Game Center |

---

## Recommended Approach for BC Arcade

These are ordered by impact-to-effort and tailored to what the codebase already has.

### Tier 1 — Minimum viable (do before submission)

**1. Arcade XP and player level**
The backend already aggregates `total_games`, `best`, and `avg` per game in `/stats/me`. A lightweight XP formula (e.g. base XP per game completed + bonus for score percentile) can be computed server-side and surfaced as a player level on the profile screen. This reuses existing data with no new game-side changes.

**2. Daily cross-game challenge**
A single daily mission that requires playing 2–3 different games (e.g. "Complete a Solitaire game and reach wave 3 in StarSwarm"). The Daily Word game already has the server-side daily puzzle infrastructure; the challenge system can reuse that pattern. This is the single highest-signal feature — it proves the app is one product, and it gives players a reason to open BC Arcade (not Blackjack, not Solitaire — *BC Arcade*) every day.

**3. Visible progression on the home screen**
The lobby should show the player's current XP level and daily challenge status prominently. Players should see their progress before choosing a game, not after.

**4. Game Center integration**
One shared Game Center leaderboard per game (all under the same app identity) plus a cross-game "Total Games Played" achievement. This is native iOS infrastructure that a website cannot replicate — it directly addresses the 4.2 concern.

**5. Notes for Review**
Before submission, write explicit review notes describing the shared systems: "Play any game to earn XP toward your player level. Today's daily challenge requires completing a Solitaire hand and a StarSwarm run. All progress persists under one profile." Reviewers spend ~5 minutes with an app; tell them exactly where to look.

---

### Tier 2 — Strong differentiators (do soon after launch)

**6. Cross-game unlock system**
Blackjack already has a working unlock system (`frontend/src/game/blackjack/unlocks.ts`) with three reward types (table_theme, card_back, chip_style). The natural next step is expanding this into a platform-wide achievement and cosmetic system — milestones in any game unlock cosmetics that apply across relevant games. This also resolves the open design question in issue #1911.

**7. Platform-wide seasonal events**
A lobby-level campaign (holiday theme, special challenge week) that applies visual theming and bonus XP across all games simultaneously. This creates the visual cohesion that signals "product" to both reviewers and players.

**8. Single premium subscription**
The entitlement JWT already gates 6 games. Reframing this as a single "BC Arcade Premium" subscription (rather than per-game unlocks) strengthens the "one product" narrative in the App Store listing and in the reviewer's experience.

---

### Tier 3 — Gold standard (backlog)

- Tiered loyalty status (Bronze → Gold → Platinum) based on Arcade XP, with visible benefits
- Cross-game challenges that unlock content in a different game than the one you played
- In-App Events published to Apple's Games app for seasonal campaigns (WWDC25 Session 215)
- Social layer via Game Center Challenges for cross-player competition

---

## Suggested Priority Order

1. Arcade XP + player level (reuses existing `/stats/me` data — low backend cost)
2. Daily cross-game challenge (highest reviewer impact; Daily Word infrastructure already exists)
3. Home screen progression display
4. Game Center leaderboard integration
5. Platform cosmetics / expand unlock system (resolves #1911)
6. Premium subscription reframing

---

## References

- [App Store Review Guidelines §4.2](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/#minimum-functionality)
- [Apple guideline 4.7 update — game streaming (Jan 2024)](https://techcrunch.com/2024/01/25/apples-app-store-now-permits-streaming-game-stores-adds-in-app-purchase-for-mini-apps-games-and-ai-chatbots/)
- [Microsoft Solitaire Collection — Daily Challenges](https://support.xbox.com/en-US/game/microsoft-casual-games/microsoft-solitaire-collection/support/all-about-daily-challenges-in-solitaire)
- [WWDC25 Session 215 — Engage players with the Apple Games app](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2025/215/)
- Related: #1911 (unlock rewards undefined)
title: Product risk: App Store guideline 4.2 — BC Arcade needs a cohesion layer before submission

If your ride 10 miles a day with the current rules you get the maximum bonus possible. This is prize-worthy! So we should track the total bonus points achieved on a leaderboard, and give a prize.

## Questions 

Is the maximum bonus 64 points? 65 points? 55 points? It depends on how you look at it.

If every mile was worth 1 point, a 10 mile ride would be 10 points with no bonus points. A 10 mile ride garners maximum bonus points - 65 instead of 10. If you look at it that way, if you ride 10 miles, 55 of those points are **bonus points**. So the maximum bonus above and beyond the 1 point per mile score is 55 points.  In a 79 day season, the max bonus points you could get would be: `79 * 55 = 4,345`

For a day with rides greater than or equal to one mile, but less than 10 miles, you'd subtract the ride length from the score to get the bonus points. For a ride day of length greater than or equal to 10 miles, you would count 55 bonus points.

This could be done similarly to the _[every day riders](https://freezingsaddles.org/people/ridedays)_ leaderboard.

### Bonus goals
It could be good if we had a graph visualizing how close people are to claiming the maximum bonus points available were.

# Whale Play — Product Requirements Document

## Problem Statement

A group of 16-20 friends run a recurring baseball stat competition called "Whale Play" in their group chat. Each game, the organizer (Neal) picks an MLB stat, a date range, and each player claims a team. Currently, Neal manually tracks scores in text messages and occasionally a Google Sheet, which is tedious, error-prone, and lacks the dramatic presentation the game deserves. There's no persistent record of past games, season standings, or cumulative rankings. The absurd comedy of the game (sweepstakes prizes, obscure stats, a "Portland Renderings" auto-win rule) has no visual home.

## Solution

A mobile-first web app that automatically fetches MLB stats from Baseball Savant, ranks players in real time, and presents results on a dramatically over-produced leaderboard — treating a contest for olive oil and bucket hats like a billion-dollar sports broadcast. The app auto-updates daily, tracks multi-game season standings with normalized scoring, and includes comedic animations, sound effects, and a nuclear "Portland Renderings" takeover easter egg. Neal configures each game via a simple Google Sheet; everything else is automated.

## User Stories

1. As a player, I want to tap a link in the group chat and instantly see the current leaderboard on my phone, so that I can check my ranking without asking Neal.
2. As a player, I want to see my rank, my team, and my stat value on the leaderboard, so that I know exactly where I stand.
3. As a player, I want to see who moved up or down since the last update, so that I can trash-talk accordingly.
4. As a player, I want to see a dramatic entrance animation when the page loads, so that opening the app feels like an event.
5. As a player, I want to see a crown animation on the current leader, so that first place feels earned.
6. As a player, I want to see a whale diving animation when someone drops 3+ spots, so that their suffering is entertaining.
7. As a player, I want to see a "tight race" indicator when the top 2 are close, so that the tension is visible.
8. As a player, I want to see a last-place shame treatment (dunce cap, glow, label), so that last place hurts.
9. As a player, I want to see Neal's game description displayed like a broadcast intro, so that his writing gets the presentation it deserves.
10. As a player, I want to see the prize displayed dramatically when it's known, so that the absurdity of the stakes is front and center.
11. As a player, I want to see a "PRIZE TBD" mystery box when the prize isn't announced yet, so that there's anticipation.
12. As a player, I want to see season standings across all Whale Plays, so that I know who's winning overall.
13. As a player, I want the season standings to use normalized points (1st = 100, scaled linearly), so that games with different player counts are weighted fairly.
14. As a player, I want to see a history of past Whale Plays with winners and prizes, so that we have a permanent record.
15. As a player, I want to tap for sound effects (air horn on leader, whale sound on last place), so that the experience is interactive without auto-playing audio.
16. As a player, I want a mute toggle for sound, so that I can control the audio.
17. As a player, I want the leaderboard to update daily without anyone doing anything, so that scores are always current.
18. As a player, I want to see a comical default avatar next to my name, so that the leaderboard has personality.
19. As Neal (organizer), I want to configure a new game by filling in a Google Sheet (game name, stat, date range, player-team assignments, prize), so that I don't need to touch code.
20. As Neal, I want to mark a game as "Final" in the sheet to close it, so that I control when a game ends (not just the date range).
21. As Neal, I want to trigger the "Portland Renderings" takeover via a toggle in the sheet, so that Heff auto-wins with a nuclear animation whenever a Portland stadium rendering appears.
22. As Neal, I want the draft order for the next game to be auto-populated from the previous game's finish, so that I don't have to calculate it.
23. As a player, I want the Portland Renderings takeover to feel like the entire site breaks — glitch effects, a stadium rendering fading in, sirens, Heff's row exploding to #1, everyone else greyed out — so that it's the funniest moment in the app.
24. As a player, I want the page to load fast on mobile (under 2 seconds), so that I don't bounce when tapping the link mid-conversation.
25. As a player, I want the app to work without logging in or creating an account, so that there's zero friction.
26. As a player on a phone, I want the leaderboard to be vertically oriented with large text and tap targets, so that it's easy to read and interact with.
27. As a player, I want the background to have subtle texture and glow effects (not flat color), so that the app feels premium and broadcast-quality.
28. As a player, I want to see the mascot (belly-flopping whale with betting slip) on the page, so that the brand is present and fun.

## Implementation Decisions

### Architecture
- **Cloudflare Pages** for static frontend hosting
- **Cloudflare Workers** for API endpoints and daily cron data fetching
- **Cloudflare KV** for data storage (current standings, game history, season standings)
- **Google Sheets API** for game configuration (read-only from the app's perspective)
- **Baseball Savant CSV exports** as primary data source
- **FanGraphs API** as secondary/fallback data source for pre-aggregated team stats

### Module Design

#### Config Reader
- Reads active game configuration from a Google Sheet via Sheets API
- Sheet structure: game name, stat description, Savant query parameters, date range, sort direction, status (Active/Final), Portland Rendering trigger, prize (optional), player nickname-team pairs
- Returns structured GameConfig objects
- Caches config in KV to reduce Sheets API calls (refreshes on cron run)

#### Data Fetcher
- Cloudflare Worker with Cron Trigger (runs daily)
- Builds Baseball Savant CSV export URL from game config parameters
- Parses CSV response, filters by date range and teams in the current game
- Aggregates raw pitch/batted-ball data to team-level stats (sum, avg, max depending on game config)
- Falls back to FanGraphs API for stats available in their pre-aggregated team leaderboard
- Stat mapping library translates human-readable stat names to Savant/FanGraphs query parameters
- Writes parsed results to KV

#### Scoring Engine
- Takes raw team stats + game config, outputs ranked leaderboard
- Handles sort direction (highest wins vs lowest wins)
- Normalized season scoring: 1st place = 100 points, last place = floor (~10), linear interpolation between based on field size
- Tie handling: tied players share the higher rank's points
- Portland Renderings override: when triggered, Heff moves to #1 regardless of stats, other players shift down
- Season standings: cumulative normalized points across all completed games

#### API Layer (Cloudflare Worker)
- `GET /api/leaderboard` — current game rankings with movement indicators (vs previous day)
- `GET /api/game` — active game metadata (name, stat, prize, Neal's write-up, date range, status)
- `GET /api/history` — completed games with final standings and winners
- `GET /api/standings` — cumulative season standings
- All endpoints return JSON, CORS-enabled

#### Frontend
- Static HTML/CSS/JS (no framework — keeps it simple, fast, and dependency-free)
- Mobile-first responsive design
- Neon Stadium color palette: #06060F primary bg, #FFE019 neon gold, #00E5FF hot cyan, #39FF14 radioactive green, #FF1744 hot red, #FF6D00 fire orange
- Background treatments by section: noise grain + neon glow (hero), CRT scanlines + cyan bleed (leaderboard), gold spotlight (prize), dot matrix (standings), noise grain (history)
- Animation system: dramatic page load entrance, crown on #1, whale dive on 3+ spot drops, tight race pulsing banner, last place shame treatment, game-over podium
- Portland Renderings takeover: full-screen glitch, stadium rendering fade-in, sirens, Heff auto-promoted, all other rows greyed, all background effects cranked to max
- Sound system: tap-to-play (air horn on leader tap, whale sound on last place), mute toggle, no auto-play
- Mascot image displayed in hero section
- Fetches from API endpoints on page load, caches in localStorage for instant re-renders

#### Storage (Cloudflare KV)
- `active-game-config` — cached game config from Google Sheet
- `active-game-rankings` — latest fetched and ranked leaderboard data (includes previous day for movement calc)
- `game-history` — JSON array of completed games with final standings
- `season-standings` — cumulative normalized points per player

### Design Direction
- 90s SportsCenter broadcast drama meets classic ballpark scoreboard
- Over-the-top fake legitimacy — billion-dollar production for sweepstakes olive oil
- Branding: "Official Whale Play™ — Est. 2023"
- Mascot: belly-flopping teal whale, red backwards cap, betting slip with BET/$$$, gold "WHALE PLAY" banner (MASCOT-FINAL.png)
- Retro block typography, bold weights, all-caps headers
- Neon glow text shadows on key stats and headers
- Comical default avatars per player (assigned, not generic)

### Google Sheet Structure
| Column | Example |
|--------|---------|
| Game Name | Going...Going...Graza Sweepstakes |
| Stat | Total Team Home Runs |
| Savant Query | stat_type=HR&aggregate=sum |
| Start Date | 2026-03-25 |
| End Date | 2026-04-05 |
| Sort | desc (highest wins) |
| Status | Active / Final |
| Prize | Graza gift bag: 2 bottles olive oil, coasters, bucket hat |
| Neal's Write-Up | (full text of his announcement) |
| Portland Rendering | FALSE |
| Player 1 Name | POC |
| Player 1 Team | LAD |
| ... | ... |

## Testing Decisions

### What makes a good test
- Test external behavior and outputs, not internal implementation
- Test edge cases that would be embarrassing to get wrong in front of 16 trash-talking friends
- Tests should be fast and runnable locally

### Modules to test

#### Scoring Engine (highest priority)
- Normalization math: verify 1st = 100, last = floor, linear interpolation
- Different field sizes produce correctly scaled points
- Tie handling: tied players share higher rank's points
- Season standings accumulation across multiple games
- Portland Renderings override: Heff goes to #1, others shift correctly
- Sort direction: highest-wins vs lowest-wins games rank correctly

#### Data Fetcher
- CSV parsing: correctly extracts team stats from Baseball Savant CSV format
- Aggregation: sum, avg, max produce correct team-level values
- Date range filtering works correctly
- Handles empty/malformed CSV responses gracefully
- FanGraphs fallback triggers when Savant query fails

### Modules NOT tested
- Config Reader — thin wrapper around Google Sheets API, tested via integration
- API Layer — thin pass-through from KV to JSON response
- Frontend — tested manually (visual/animation correctness is subjective)

## Out of Scope

- User accounts, authentication, or login
- In-app draft/team selection (happens in the group chat)
- Real-time updates (daily is sufficient)
- Custom player avatars (future feature — defaults only for v1)
- Multi-sport support (architecture is sport-agnostic but v1 is baseball only)
- Push notifications or alerts

The AIB tournament pages (`/aib/2024/q3` through `/aib/2025/fall`) are heavily duplicated. Each quarter has its own near-identical copy of every component — page-view, hero, cards, and leaderboard — with only small data differences (quarter label, start date, image URL, tournament slug). 1. **Define a per-tournament config object** with all the differences (quarter label, year, image URL, date/prize translation keys, tournament slug, etc.) so adding a new tournament is just a new entry.

## Why
Currently only free-for-all exists, which limits replayability and player preferences. Different modes provide:
- Variety and freshness
- Different strategic approaches
- Team-based cooperation
- Unique challenges and goals
- Broader appeal to different player types
- Tournament and competitive diversity

## Scope

### Teams Mode
- **2v2, 3v3, 4v4**: Fixed team sizes
- **Team Colors**: Distinct colors for each team
- **Team Scoring**: Combined team mass or team kills
- **Friendly Fire**: Option to enable/disable
- **Team Chat**: Private chat for team members
- **Team Spawning**: Spawn near teammates
- **Win Condition**: Team with highest combined mass or last team standing

### Battle Royale
- **Shrinking Zone**: Playable area shrinks over time
- **Zone Damage**: Players outside zone take damage/lose mass
- **Last Player Standing**: Win by being the last alive
- **Loot Drops**: Random powerups spawn in the zone
- **Tension Building**: Zone shrinks faster as player count decreases
- **Victory Royale**: Special screen/effects for winner

### Limited-Time Events
- **Daily Challenges**: Special rules for 24 hours
  - "Mass x2" day
  - "Speed boost" day
  - "No splitting" day
  - "Tiny map" day
- **Weekly Tournaments**: Competitive events with prizes
- **Seasonal Events**: Holiday-themed modes (Halloween, Christmas, etc.)
- **Custom Rules**: Rotating special rules each day

### Custom Game Settings
- **Map Size**: Small, medium, large, huge
- **Player Count**: 10, 25, 50, 100 players
- **Bot Count**: Adjust number of AI players
- **Powerup Frequency**: Low, normal, high, extreme
- **Growth Rate**: Slow, normal, fast, extreme
- **Split Cooldown**: None, short, normal, long
- **Zone Effects**: Enable/disable zone mechanics
- **Private Matches**: Password-protected lobbies

### Special Modes
- **King of the Hill**: Control center zone for points
- **Capture the Flag**: Steal enemy team's flag and return to base
- **Infection**: One "zombie" player, others try to survive
- **Prop Hunt**: Some players hide as objects, others seek
- **Freeze Tag**: Tagged players freeze, teammates can unfreeze
- **Mass Race**: First to reach X mass wins

### Mode Selection UI
- **Mode Browser**: Browse available modes with descriptions
- **Quick Play**: Matchmake into random mode
- **Mode Rotation**: Show current and upcoming modes
- **Favorites**: Save preferred modes for quick access
- **Mode Statistics**: Track wins/losses per mode

### Mode-Specific Features
- **Leaderboards**: Separate leaderboards for each mode
- **Achievements**: Mode-specific achievements
- **Unlockables**: Mode-specific cosmetics
- **Ranking System**: ELO or skill-based ranking per mode
