- [ ] Team colors and scoring work correctly
- [ ] Battle royale mode with shrinking zone
- [ ] Zone damage works for battle royale
- [ ] At least 3 limited-time event types
- [ ] Custom game settings are configurable
- [ ] Private matches with password protection
- [ ] Mode selection UI is intuitive
- [ ] Separate leaderboards per mode
- [ ] Mode-specific achievements work
- [ ] At least 2 special modes implemented

## Technical Notes
- Game mode system needs to be modular and extensible
- Each mode needs its own win condition logic
- Team mode needs team state management
- Battle royale needs zone physics and damage system
- Custom settings need validation and balance
- Mode rotation needs scheduling system
- Consider server load for different modes
- Some modes may require new mechanics (flags, objectives, etc.)

```tsx
import { dummyEvents } from "../utils/types/events";

// src/pages/index.tsx:110
<RecentEvents events={dummyEvents} />
```

The `getServerSideProps` function (lines 252–405) fetches all 6 active leaderboards and prizes in parallel, but **never calls the backend endpoint that returns recent completed tournament data**. The same issue exists in `src/pages/dashboard.tsx:39` and `src/pages/leaderboard.tsx` (which even has a `// TODO: Figure out how to actually fetch events later` comment).

The two hardcoded placeholder events in `src/utils/types/events.ts` are:
- "Single Player Daily Tournament" — September 17, 2025
- "Multiplayer Daily Tournament" — September 18, 2025

## Backend API Available

The backend already supports this via `GET /api/v2/tournament/summary?includeWinners=true`, which returns a `recentWinners` array from `TournamentService.getRecentMetadata()`. That method queries the `tournament_metadata` table for the 10 most recent completed tournaments (status = `'completed'`, `winningTime != null`), ordered by `endDate DESC`.

`tournamentApi.getTournamentSummary()` already exists in `src/services/tournamentApi.ts` and can be used to call this endpoint.

## Fix

In `getServerSideProps` in `src/pages/index.tsx`:
1. Add a call to `tournamentApi.getTournamentSummary({ includeWinners: true })` in the `Promise.all` block.
2. Map the `recentWinners` response to the `TournamentEvent[]` shape expected by `<RecentEvents>`.
3. Pass the real events to `<RecentEvents>` instead of `dummyEvents`.
4. Apply the same fix to `dashboard.tsx` and `leaderboard.tsx`.
5. Remove or deprecate `dummyEvents` from `src/utils/types/events.ts` once real data is wired up.

## Files Affected

- `src/pages/index.tsx` — line 4 (import), line 110 (usage), `getServerSideProps` (no fetch)
- `src/pages/dashboard.tsx` — line 39
- `src/pages/leaderboard.tsx`
- `src/utils/types/events.ts` — `dummyEvents` constant to be removed
- `src/services/tournamentApi.ts` — `getTournamentSummary()` already exists, just needs to be called

#### Summary

Add a **“Kiosk” or “Booth Display” mode** to `quiz.opensuse.org` — a **fullscreen, widescreen-optimized layout** for use at openSUSE booths during events.

This mode should combine the existing `/stats` functionality with a visually appealing **public dashboard** that shows:

* the **live leaderboard** (top participants and scores),
* a large **QR code** for visitors to join the quiz,
* and a **locally configurable message and prize draw time**.

It should also provide booth staff with quick access to:

* a **reset link** (secured with a token prompt), and
* a **link to `/bingo`** for random winner selection during prize draws.

---

### 🎯 Purpose

* Provide an attractive, widescreen display at openSUSE booths.
* Encourage visitors to scan the QR code and participate.
* Allow booth crew to configure local details (like “Win a Raspberry Pi 5!” and prize draw time) without backend or URL parameters.
* Give staff convenient access to operational tools (`/reset`, `/bingo`) during the event.

---

### 🧩 Suggested URL

`https://quiz.opensuse.org/booth`
(or `/kiosk`)

Each event runs as its own instance, so no query parameters are needed — configuration is stored locally in the browser.

---

### 🧱 Suggested Layout (Widescreen Mockup)

```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 🦎  openSUSE Quiz Live @ [Event Name]                    ⏰ Prize Draw: 15:30  │

│                                                                               │
│     [⚙️ Settings]      [🔁 Reset Quiz]      [🎲 Open Bingo / Pick Winner]     │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Layout overview:**

* **Left:** real-time leaderboard (auto-updating from `/stats`)
* **Right:** large scannable QR code and join message
* **Top:** event name and prize draw time
* **Bottom:** local message, plus small admin controls for booth crew

---

### ⚙️ Implementation Details

* **Endpoint:** `/booth` or `/kiosk`

* **Data source:** reuse existing `/stats` JSON or WebSocket feed

* **Auto-refresh:** every 15–30 seconds

* **Local Configuration (via Cookie):**

  * Booth crew sets:

    * `Prize Draw Time` (e.g., 15:30)
    * `Custom Message` (e.g., “Win a Raspberry Pi 5!”)
  * Stored locally in the browser’s cookie or localStorage.
  * Configurable via a small ⚙️ **Settings panel** (bottom corner).
  * Values persist across reloads until `/reset` is triggered.

* **Reset Functionality:**

  * Add a `[🔁 Reset Quiz]` link/button.
  * When clicked, it asks for a **reset token** before executing `/reset`.
  * Useful for daily resets or end-of-day cleanups.

* **Bingo Integration:**

* Special currency used only during the tournament
* Each Smily vote in the tournament costs **10 Points**
* Points will reset or expire after the tournament ends
* Source: Points are auto-granted (e.g., 1000 Points on registration) or can be earned via referral or participation

### 3\. 🏆 **Winner Takes All**

* **Single Winner**: Player with the **highest tournament score** by 6:30 PM
* **Prize Money**: ₹10,000 (starting point, can vary)
* Admin configurable prize pool

### 4\. 📝 **Registration / Walk-in Join**

* Users must **Register** or click **“Join Walk-in”** during the tournament period
* Only registered players can earn tournament scores

### 5\. 📊 **Leaderboard Tab**

* Real-time leaderboard showing:
  * Rank
  * Username
  * Points spent
  * Games won
  * Tournament Score
* Sort options: Top Score, Most Wins, Recent Joiners

### 6\. 🪧 **Tournament Banner + Themes**

* Banner on Home, Wallet, and Tournament Tabs
* Themes rotate weekly or by admin:
  * “Happy Hours”
  * “Millionaire”
  * “Weekend Bonanza”
* Admin-configurable: Banner image, name, description, prize

### 7\. 📣 **Marketing & Promotions**

* In-app promo push at 5:45 PM daily
* Special weekly banners for “Weekend Bonanza”
* Shareable wins for virality

---

## User Flow

1. **Pre-Tournament (5:45 PM–6:00 PM)**
   * Users see banner on home
   * Receive push notification
   * Option to **Pre-register**
2. **During Tournament (6:00–6:30 PM)**
   * User taps **“Join Now”**
   * Auto-receive Points (e.g. 100)
   * Plays Smily Game multiple times
   * Leaderboard updates in real-time
3. **Post-Tournament (6:30 PM)**
   * Winner announced
   * Leaderboard frozen
   * Prize disbursed (e.g. within 1 hr)
   * Option to share win or “Remind Me Tomorrow”

---

## Edge Cases & Safeguards

* Users joining at 6:29 PM get fewer gameplay chances — expected behavior
* Handle server load spikes during join/play
* Points should expire after tournament to avoid hoarding
* Disqualification logic for suspicious behavior (optional future)

---

## Design Needs

* Tournament banner carousel
* “Join Walk-in” modal
* In-game Points balance UI
* Leaderboard tab & toggle
* End-of-tournament results screen
* Shareable winner screen

body:
# Play Off The Grid

## Overview

Play Off The Grid is a special account option for individuals who wish to participate in HavaGr8Day while sharing little or no personal information.

This option is intended for special circumstances and is not part of the standard registration process.

Play Off The Grid accounts allow participants to enjoy the full HavaGr8Day experience using a nickname and password while minimizing the amount of personal information stored within the system.

## Purpose

Some individuals have legitimate privacy concerns regarding:

* Personal information stored online
* Email collection
* AI systems
* Data sharing
* Public identity visibility

Play Off The Grid provides a privacy-focused alternative while still allowing full participation in the HavaGr8Day movement.

## How It Works

Individuals interested in Play Off The Grid participation must contact an administrator directly.

If approved, an administrator will create the account and provide login credentials.

Typical information required:

* Nickname
* Password

Optional information:

* Name
* Email Address

## Gameplay

Play Off The Grid participants receive the same core game experience as all other players.

They may:

* Play Bingo
* Complete Deeds
* Use Quick Actions
* Join Teams
* Earn Bingos
* Unlock Levels
* Contribute to the Impact Board
* Participate in Team activities

## Privacy

Play Off The Grid accounts are designed to minimize stored personal information.

The system should not require:

* First Name
* Last Name
* Email Address

Participation is based primarily on a nickname and password.

## Password Recovery

Because Play Off The Grid accounts may not contain contact information, automated password recovery is not available.

If a participant forgets their credentials, they must contact an administrator directly for assistance.

## Benefits

* Supports privacy-conscious participants
* Minimizes personal information collection
* Eliminates anonymous registration spam concerns
* Maintains administrative oversight
* Preserves the full HavaGr8Day experience
* Accommodates special circumstances without complicating the standard registration process

## Key Principle

Play Off The Grid is a privacy-focused participation option available in special circumstances through administrator approval.

# Claude Code Prompt: Play Off The Grid Accounts

Build a new admin-created account type called **Play Off The Grid**.

This is a privacy-focused player account option for special circumstances.

It is **not** a public registration option.

## Core Requirement

Only administrators can create Play Off The Grid accounts.

Players should not see Play Off The Grid as a standard registration choice.

## Account Type

Add or update account type support:

* standard
* off_grid
* admin

Player-facing label:

**Play Off The Grid**

Internal value can be:

`off_grid`

## Account Creation

In Admin Player Management, add:

**Create Play Off The Grid Player**

Required fields:

* Nickname
* Password or temporary password

Optional fields:

* First Name
* Last Name
* Email Address
* Team
* Status
* Selected Play Level

Do not require email.

Do not require first name or last name.

Nickname must be unique.

## Login

Play Off The Grid players log in using:

* Nickname
* Password

They must not be required to use email.

## Gameplay Access

Play Off The Grid players must be able to:

* Play Bingo
* Complete deeds
* Use Quick Actions
* Join Teams
* Earn Bingos
* Unlock Levels
* Contribute to the Impact Board
* Participate in Team activity

## Display Rules

When displaying a player:

1. If nickname exists, show nickname.
2. Else if name exists, show full name.
3. Else show Player #[id].

Leaderboards should show nickname for Play Off The Grid players.

## Password Recovery

Automated password recovery is not available unless an email exists.

If a Play Off The Grid player uses Forgot Password and no email exists, display:

"Please contact an administrator for help recovering your Play Off The Grid account."

Admin must be able to reset the password manually.

## Prize Eligibility

Add field:

`eligible_for_prizes`

Default for Play Off The Grid accounts:

`false`

Admin may override if needed.

## Admin Management

Admin Player Management should allow admins to:

* View Play Off The Grid players
* Search/filter by account type
* Edit nickname
* Edit optional name/email
* Change team
* Change status
* Reset password
* Deactivate account

## Security

Only admins can create or modify Play Off The Grid account type.

Do not expose password hashes.

Protect all admin endpoints.

Add audit logging for:

* Play Off The Grid account created
* Password reset
* Team changed
* Account deactivated
* Prize eligibility changed

## Existing Users

Do not break existing standard players.

Do not require migration of existing players unless needed to support the account type field.

## Testing

Verify:

* Admin can create Play Off The Grid player
* Email is not required
* Name is not required
* Nickname must be unique
* Player can log in with nickname/password
* Player can play normally
* Player can complete deeds
* Player can use Quick Actions
* Player can join Teams
* Player appears by nickname on leaderboards
* Impact Board stats remain accurate
* Forgot Password shows admin-contact message when no email exists
* Admin can reset password
* Prize eligibility defaults to false
* Existing standard players still work

## Final Goal

SUGGESTED CLAUDE CODE

A privacy-sensitive participant should be able to play HavaGr8Day using a nickname and password, with the account created and managed by an administrator, while preserving the full gameplay experience and avoiding public anonymous registration.
